title: Which vaccinations are recommended in Germany?
intro: In Germany, the Standing Committee on Vaccination (STIKO) at the Robert Koch Institute publishes recommendations for children, adults and special groups. They are updated regularly, so check the current schedule with your doctor. This overview is general and does not replace the official schedule.

sections.heading: Infants and children
paragraphs: Standard vaccinations in the first years include rotavirus, diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, Haemophilus influenzae type b, polio, hepatitis B, pneumococcus, meningococcus, measles, mumps, rubella and chickenpox. Doses are given at specific ages, such as from two months, and boosters follow. Children usually receive them at routine check-ups.

sections.heading: Adolescents
paragraphs: Boosters for tetanus, diphtheria, whooping cough and polio are recommended in adolescence. Vaccination against human papillomavirus (HPV) is recommended for girls and boys from about nine to fourteen, with catch-up possible until seventeen. Any missing doses of measles, mumps, rubella, hepatitis B and chickenpox should be caught up.

sections.heading: Adults
paragraphs: Adults should have a tetanus and diphtheria booster every ten years, with one dose including whooping cough. People born after 1970 who have not been vaccinated or only once against measles should be vaccinated. Older adults from sixty are advised to have yearly influenza vaccination, pneumococcal vaccination, shingles vaccination and COVID-19 vaccination according to current advice.

sections.heading: Special groups
paragraphs: Pregnant women are advised to be vaccinated against whooping cough and influenza. Healthcare workers, people with chronic illnesses, weak immunity, and travellers have additional recommendations, such as hepatitis A and B, tick-borne encephalitis in risk areas, and travel vaccines. Your doctor can advise on these.

sections.heading: Practical points
paragraphs: Bring your vaccination card or yellow booklet to appointments. Statutory health insurance covers recommended vaccinations. Vaccines are very well monitored for safety, and side effects are usually mild, such as sore arm or low fever. If you lost your records, a doctor can advise how to catch up.

examples.title: Checking your record
examples.text: Imagine you have an old vaccination booklet. You could take it to your doctor and ask what is missing.

examples.title: Planning for travel
examples.text: Suppose you plan a trip abroad. You might ask your doctor or a travel clinic several weeks before departure.
